posts: Most digital products are already being sold badly — through DMs, screenshots of payment apps, and a trust-me-I'll-send-it-after arrangement. The thing being sold is usually worth less than the friction of checking out 🧵

1/ Four shapes come up constantly: betting picks, your trades, content you make, and files or templates. What they share isn't a category — it's that a card checkout costs more than the item is worth.

2/ Picks and trade calls are the clearest case for settling in seconds, because both DECAY. A pick is worth something before kickoff and nothing after. An entry level is worth something before the move.
3/ Any rail that takes days to clear — or can reverse weeks later — is a poor fit for a product whose entire value is that it arrived in time.
4/ And the audience for both already holds a wallet. So the thing that usually kills a small sale — make an account, enter a card — is already solved before you start.

5/ Content and files run on different logic: not urgency, price. Charging $2 for one essay or one template is uneconomic on a rail with fixed per-transaction costs. Per-item pricing only works if the overhead of a single sale is near zero.

6/ Mechanically: price it in a stablecoin so neither side guesses, list it somewhere a wallet can pay directly, and let on-chain settlement BE the confirmation — rather than waiting on a card network to clear.
7/ One thing most write-ups skip: settling the payment and delivering the file are different problems. A storefront that nails the first and leaves the second to a Discord DM isn't finished.

8/ And buyers increasingly aren't human. Every SmartSite is an x402 storefront — a product you add is automatically payable by AI agents in USDC, with payout going on-chain to you. No checkout form to fill in.

9/ Caveat worth stating: selling info about betting or trading is subject to the rules where you and your buyer live. The rail settles the sale; it doesn't license the business. https://www.swopme.co/blog/sell-digital-products-for-crypto
